official.deadline_note: No application closing date is published on any AUW admissions page. AUW intakes students three times per year - Spring (class starts in January), Summer (May) and Fall (September) - and every admissions page carries the banner 'ADMISSIONS ARE OPEN!'. For transfer applications, the deadline depends on the applicant's desired start date.
official.application_cycle: Three intakes per year: Spring (class starts January), Summer (May), Fall (September)
official.status_note: Every AUW admissions page currently carries the banner 'ADMISSIONS ARE OPEN!' with no closing date stated.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Full scholarships cover tuition, room and board, course supplies, student activities, and primary healthcare. AUW states it 'waives ALL fees and covers all costs for students who are first in their family to enter university and those who enter Asian University for Women through Pathways for Promise program.' Tuition alone is published at US$9,000 per year.

Information from a third party source(s) as needed, and other document(s)/information as the committee deems necessary
selection_criteria: Need-blind admissions: AUW seeks women who show high potential, leadership qualities and strong motivation regardless of their economic background

Holistic review focusing on academic excellence, leadership potential and personal context as demonstrated by prior academic performance, extracurricular and community activities, and personal statement

Financial Aid Committee assessment of family circumstances: family composition, parents' education level, jobs and professions of earning members, income of parents/guardians and other supporting members, number of non-earning dependents, movable and immovable property at present market value, community's comment on socio-economic status, schooling costs of the student and her siblings, socio-economic situation of the area of residence, and luxury items owned
coverage: Books, course supplies, student activities: US$3,000 per year
Room and board: US$3,000 per year
It costs US$15,000 to send a student to AUW for one year, irrespective of academic program; these fees include all tuition, room and board, books, course supplies, healthcare and student activities
Travel grants for qualifying international students on financial aid: a one-way ticket to Chittagong and a ticket home after graduation from AUW
application_method: Submit the application through AUW's online admission portal
Submit the applicable Self-Assessment Form with all supporting financial documents as part of the admission application
Shortlisted applicants sit a locally administered entrance examination (English grammar, reading, writing and Math) followed by a personal interview
All financial aid awards are assessed prior to the beginning of each academic program (Pathways for Promise or the Undergraduate Program) and are confirmed in the offer letter
official.application_route: Apply online through AUW's admission portal; financial aid is assessed as part of the admission application via the Self-Assessment Form and confirmed in the offer letter
official.study_mode: Full-time; residential, with room and board published as part of the annual cost
official.citizenship_residency: AUW is required under its Charter to make reasonable efforts to recruit young women primarily from South, Southeast, West Asia and the Middle East; the University also accepts stateless students and exchange students from the United States, Europe and East Asia, as well as others from outside Asia.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - international students are eligible, and travel grants may be awarded to international students who qualify for financial assistance
official.duration: Four academic years for students entering directly into the undergraduate program; a student entering through the Pre-Undergraduate/Pathways program ordinarily requires five years to graduate. Financial aid is assessed prior to each academic program and continued year by year subject to maintaining a CGPA of 2.5.
official.description: AUW strives to meet the demonstrated financial need of each admitted student and offers full and partial scholarships based on each student's financial circumstances; full scholarships cover tuition, room and board, course supplies, student activities, and primary healthcare. Currently 85% of AUW students receive scholarship support, and the majority of women currently enrolled are on full scholarship.
official.program_type: University need-based scholarship and financial aid (full and partial), awarded as part of admission
official.english_requirement: A minimum score of 60% in English in the final examinations of grade X & XII (with equivalent grades accepted for other examination systems); the language of instruction at AUW is English. No IELTS/TOEFL requirement is published.

not_confirmed: Per-student award amount: financial aid is individually assessed by the Financial Aid Committee and no fixed award figure is published; the recorded amount is AUW's published full annual cost of attendance (US$15,000) that full scholarships cover
Application deadline date: no closing date is published on AUW's pages
IELTS/TOEFL or other standardized English test requirement: not published on AUW's admissions pages
verification.notes: All figures and rules were taken from the awarding body's own admissions pages on asian-university.org (scholarships-financial-aid, tuition-fees, who-can-apply, how-to-apply, FAQ); no aggregator or third-party values were used.

applicant_utility.summary: AUW folds financial aid into the admission application, so there is no separate scholarship to win: you file the Self-Assessment Form with your financial evidence alongside the admission form on AUW's online portal. Full awards cover the entire published US$15,000 annual cost of attendance - tuition, room and board, books and supplies, activities, and healthcare - and because aid is need-based rather than merit-based, the strength and consistency of your financial documentation matters as much as your grades. Nothing about the award is fixed in advance, and the committee verifies every declaration you make.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Women from low-income households across South, Southeast and West Asia and the Middle East - especially first-generation university students and Pathways for Promise entrants, whose fees AUW waives entirely.
application_readiness_checklist: Verify early that you clear 60% individually in English and in Maths in the final Grade X and Grade XII examinations, and that you are within 22 years of age

Complete the correct Self-Assessment Form version - SAF-Bangladesh if applying from Bangladesh, SAF-International otherwise - and attach bank statements, tax returns and salary certificates before submitting
Prepare for a locally administered entrance exam in English grammar, reading, writing and Math plus a personal interview after shortlisting
Budget for the one-time US$600 admission fee and US$200 refundable caution deposit, which are not covered by default
Email admissions@auw.edu.bd to confirm intake timing for your desired start month, since no closing date is published
common_rejection_risks: Falling below 60% in English or Maths in the Grade X/XII finals - these are hard individual cut-offs, not averages
Incomplete or inconsistent SAF financial evidence - the committee investigates and verifies all submitted information, including property, sibling earnings and luxury items
Being over 22 years of age at the time of application
Applying as a transfer student and assuming aid follows you - transfer students are ineligible for financial aid
Expecting aid to be increased after enrolment: later increases require a major event that severely changed the family's finances and are a rare occurrence
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: A one-time admission fee of US$600 (waivable at the Financial Aid Committee's discretion) and a US$200 refundable caution deposit apply to admitted students and are not covered by default; personal spending is not addressed, and travel home during intermediate summers is not covered - the travel grant is limited to a one-way ticket to Chittagong plus a ticket home after graduation, with intermediate-summer travel expected to be funded through work-study wages.
document_audit: Pick the correct SAF version - SAF-Bangladesh vs SAF-International - a wrong version can stall the file
Salary certificates must cover every salaried parent, and bank statements should cover the period the committee asks about
Declare everything: family property, siblings' earnings, school fees paid and household items are all cross-checked, and undeclared assets can sink an aid package
Keep Finance Department receipts for every payment - they are required for any future refund, including the caution deposit
alerts: No closing date is published and AUW intakes three times a year (January, May, September starts); confirm intake timing before making travel or work plans
A CGPA of 2.5 must be maintained every single year or financial aid is not continued
Choosing to reside and take meals outside AUW facilities removes the US$3,000 room-and-board charge, which changes assessed need
Late fee payment attracts a flat BDT 1,000 fine plus 2% per month on the due amount
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Online portal application plus SAF and financial documents, then shortlisting, a locally administered entrance exam and interview, with the aid package confirmed in the offer letter before enrolment.
